title: The Sentry scrub rewrites random ids: about 1 in 200 events gets event_id, trace_id, span_id or parent_span_id mangled
evidence: scrubEventText runs scrubText's METRIC_THEN_VALUE_RE (app/lib/instrument-scrub.mjs ~:334, applied ~:349) over every string in the event, ids included; the lab-name list holds hex-only names (e1, e2, b12), so an id starting with one of them followed by digits loses the digits to [value]. Measured over 200,000 random 32-hex ids: 0.495% rewritten (e1 511, e2 446, b12 33). Affects every server event's event_id, contexts.trace.trace_id, span_id and parent_span_id. No privacy leak (the scrub only removes characters); a mangled body trace_id stops matching the never-scrubbed envelope header's trace_id, so trace linking breaks for that event. Found by PR 1289's CI. Owner ruled option A (skip the id fields in scrubEventText, with the parity edit in health-core sentry-scrub.ts), assigned to the untangle audit builder (scrubber generation series), security class: adversary + Codex.
